weeks.headline: Wind output builds sharply from tonight and peaks on Tuesday, when Elexon's national forecast reaches about 19.9 GW around midday, before easing to roughly 13 GW by Wednesday evening. From Thursday the picture is patchier, with breezy conditions in the north and light winds in the south and east, and the weekend looks light and overcast. Confidence falls beyond about Thursday.
weeks.summary: A windy Tuesday opens the week, then high pressure keeps things cold, cloudy and only moderately breezy.

weeks.table_note: Wind speeds are Met Office coastal and inland 10 m forecasts for the named towns, which understate hub-height wind. Monday figures cover 07:00 onwards. Elexon figures are national wind forecasts and run to Wednesday evening only.

buyers.label: High-wind periods
buyers.text: Late Monday into Wednesday is the most likely window for softer day-ahead and overnight prices, with curtailment and Scottish transmission constraints possible at the Tuesday peak. Output at that level can also pull evening-peak prices down, though demand and gas prices will still matter.

buyers.label: Low-wind risk
buyers.text: Monday morning starts with national wind output near 4.5 GW, and Saturday and Sunday look light and overcast. Gas is likely to fill the gap in those periods, which tends to firm prices, especially at the evening peak. Weekend demand is lower, which may soften the effect.

buyers.label: Demand
buyers.text: Temperatures of roughly 0 to 9°C and frost midweek support heating demand. The Met Office long-range outlook for late November and early December has high pressure from the north-east, temperatures often below average and a greater than normal chance of snow to lower levels.

buyers.label: For buyers
buyers.text: Those on flexible or day-ahead-linked contracts carry the most exposure to a swing from a windy Tuesday to a lighter weekend. These are likely tendencies based on the forecast, not certainties or advice.

areas.title: Offshore wind (North Sea and Irish Sea)
areas.text: Moray Firth (Beatrice, Moray East) is the windiest zone all week: Wick forecasts 19-26 mph on Tuesday, 15-27 mph on Thursday and 15-28 mph on Friday, with gusts of 48 to 50 mph. That stays below the roughly 55 mph storm cut-out level, so no cut-out risk is flagged. In the Irish Sea (Walney, West of Duddon Sands), the shipping forecast has a gale warning for southeasterly force 8 later on Monday.

areas.title: Scotland onshore wind and hydro
areas.text: Wick is the strongest of the onshore proxies. Tuesday is the peak, and Wednesday to Friday stay moderate. Rain and hill snow linger over Scotland on Wednesday, and a band of rain stalls over western Scotland on Tuesday, which should help hydro inflows, although precipitation falling as snow on higher ground is held back until a thaw.

areas.title: Wales and northern England
areas.text: Mid Wales onshore wind looks very weak, with Llandrindod Wells at 1-8 mph all week and a top gust of 27 mph on Tuesday. Northern England fares better, with Barrow and Bridlington reaching moderate levels on Tuesday and again on Friday. Frost is likely in Wales and parts of the east on Monday and Wednesday.

areas.title: Solar (south and east England)
areas.text: Cambridge has sunny spells on Monday after morning fog, and sunny intervals on Tuesday and Wednesday. Thursday to Sunday is cloudy or overcast, with maximums of 4 to 6°C. Winter solar output is modest at best, so this adds little to the picture on any day.

watch.text: Gale-force south-easterlies in the Irish Sea, Malin and Hebrides sea areas, and Elexon's forecast climbing to about 12.5 GW by midnight.

weeks.caveats: All seven location pages were current (first date 23 November). The Met Office warnings page carried a notice that warnings may be out of date, so the "no warnings" reading is unconfirmed. A search for reputable market commentary returned nothing usable and none is cited.

weeks.headline: A cold, fairly calm start gives way to a windy Tuesday, when Elexon's national forecast peaks at about 20.7 GW. Winds then ease through Wednesday and look light from Thursday to Saturday, with frost, before Atlantic fronts return on Sunday.
weeks.summary: One strong wind day, then a likely three-day low-wind, cold spell. Confidence drops sharply after Thursday.

weeks.table_note: Ratings are based on coastal 10 m winds, which understate hub-height wind, plus Elexon national forecasts to Wednesday only. Thursday to Sunday ratings rest mainly on forecast gusts, as hourly wind speeds were not available. Mid Wales and Highland data were unavailable, so the onshore column uses Dunbar and Barrow as a guide.

buyers.label: High-wind periods
buyers.text: Tuesday's wind peak of about 20.7 GW could weigh on day-ahead and overnight prices. Scottish transmission constraints and some curtailment are possible, though any price effect is likely to be short.

buyers.label: Low-wind risk
buyers.text: Thursday to Saturday looks lighter and colder. Gas would fill the gap, which tends to firm day-ahead and evening-peak prices, especially on cold, dark evenings. Confidence is low this far out.

buyers.label: Demand
buyers.text: Frost on Thursday and Friday (down to -2°C at Cambridge) would lift heating demand, while the Saturday weekend would offset part of that.

buyers.label: For buyers
buyers.text: Day-to-day swings are mainly relevant to flexible and index-linked contracts. The Met Office outlook for 20-29 November points to Atlantic systems and possible strong winds, which could ease the later picture. Treat all of this as tendencies, not certainties.

areas.title: Offshore wind (North Sea and Irish Sea)
areas.text: Coastal winds near Hornsea and Dogger Bank (Bridlington) and the East Anglia zone (Lowestoft) reach 22 mph and 20 mph on Tuesday, with gusts of 45 and 44 mph. That is strong output but below the roughly 55 mph storm cut-out level. The Irish Sea (Walney, West of Duddon Sands) is the one to watch: the shipping forecast has southeasterly gale force 8 expected there, perhaps severe gale 9 later, so localised cut-outs are possible late Monday into Tuesday.

areas.title: Scotland onshore wind and hydro
areas.text: Forth and Cromarty sea areas see force 4 to 6, occasionally 7, on Monday. Both Wick forecast pages were out of date, so there is no Moray Firth or Highlands read this week. Highland rainfall figures were not available, so there is no hydro view this week.

areas.title: Wales and northern England
areas.text: The Llandrindod Wells page was stale, so Mid Wales has no direct read. Barrow-in-Furness shows 6-22 mph on Tuesday with 45 mph gusts, falling to 7-9 mph on Wednesday. Yellow snow warnings cover high ground in Yorkshire and Humber, the North East and the North West on Tuesday morning.

areas.title: Solar (south and east England)
areas.text: Winter output is modest. Cambridge is sunny on Monday, wet on Tuesday and brighter on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday. Cloud on Thursday and rain on Sunday keep solar low.
